notes: BIG: preview now matches the final render exactly. Caption layout (which words go in each caption + line breaks + timing) is computed by ONE engine on the server (build_timeline) and the preview just draws it — no more drift between the on-screen preview and the burned render. Styling (colours, stroke, shadow, scrim, karaoke, animation) stays instant client-side; layout refreshes on a short debounce like the exact preview, with a local fallback for the demo/pre-transcription placeholder. Also in this build: default presets baked into the app (whole team always has the library); the beta Animation can't hide captions; the last caption no longer hangs to the clip end on the board/merged path; Export names captioned files with the _nSub suffix removed; Export/Import a style as .json to share; green Export button. Fix: applying a preset now actually switches the font everywhere — the dropdown, the live preview and the render all follow the preset's font (before, a stale font could override it, so a preset showed one font but rendered another). Fix: editing captions in the Words tab now flows to the Text tab, the preview and the export — both tabs and the render share one word source, so your Words-tab edits are always burned in. Fix: Enter caption breaks are no longer lost on the way to the render — every path that prepares words (Assemble, board, hook save, LOC, export) now reads the breaks straight from your text like the preview does, instead of only inheriting older ones. Assemble: exporting from Edit no longer drops a duplicate of that clip into the Hooks column. Typewriter captions are now REAL, not just a preview: with Animation = Typewriter the words appear one by one in the final render too (the other animation styles stay preview-only/beta for now). New: Settings → Assembly cache shows how much disk the normalized clips use, with a Clear cache button. New: '⚙ Normalize' next to Export — prepares a 'wild' clip (straight out of Kling / Freepik / Higgsfield: 720p, 24fps, odd audio) for assembly without captions: it's conformed to the project format, added to the board, and then joins other segments by stream copy instead of re-encoding. Speed: a finished body is no longer re-encoded for every creative. Each clip is normalized once (cached in ~/.assembler/cache) and creatives are then assembled with stream copy — measurably faster on batches (1.6x on a 4 hooks + 30s body test, and the gain grows with body length and hook count) and the body keeps its original quality instead of losing a generation per render. Safety kept: any clip whose parameters don't match is normalized first, the result is length-verified, and anything suspicious silently falls back to the old full re-encode. Board render now also reports the batch timing (total, per creative, creatives/min, realtime factor) and logs it. New: a built-in render speed test (Settings → Run speed test) — renders the loaded clip a few times, optionally several at once, and reports realtime factor + clips/min for that Mac. Anyone on the team can run it, so capacity planning gets numbers from several real machines. New: render benchmark for capacity planning — tools/benchmark.py measures your real creatives (realtime factor + how throughput scales when rendering N at once) and writes a CSV. Every render/assemble also appends a durable timing row to ~/.assembler/timings.csv, so numbers no longer vanish with the on-screen timer. New: 'Headline · text overlay' — a static text block burned over the video (size, colour, vertical position, outline, optional plate, show from/to). It stays TEXT, so each language keeps its own copy: type the headline per language and every language version renders with its own line. Preview shows it live; Export and the board bake it in. New on the board: a small ▸ on any hook tile reuses that clip as a Body part, so you can build hook + hook + hook (not only hook + a library body).
